events.title: Christopher Latham Sholes Patents the Typewriter
events.description: Christopher Latham Sholes, together with Carlos Glidden and Samuel Soule, received a U.S. patent for a practical typewriter in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. The design was later sold to E. Remington and Sons, who began mass-producing it in 1873.
events.significance: The typewriter transformed office work and written communication, and the QWERTY layout from Sholes's design remains the standard keyboard arrangement today.

events.title: Birth of Alan Turing
events.description: Alan Mathison Turing was born in Maida Vale, London. He became a mathematician and logician who formalized the concepts of algorithm and computation with the Turing machine and played a key role in breaking the German Enigma cipher during World War II at Bletchley Park.
events.significance: Turing is widely regarded as the father of theoretical computer science and artificial intelligence, and his wartime codebreaking helped shorten World War II.

events.title: Battle of Plassey
events.description: Forces of the British East India Company under Robert Clive defeated the Nawab of Bengal, Siraj ud-Daulah, at Plassey. The victory was aided by the defection of Mir Jafar, the Nawab's commander.
events.significance: The battle established British East India Company dominance in Bengal and marked a key step toward British colonial rule over the Indian subcontinent.

events.title: Title IX Signed into Law
events.description: President Richard Nixon signed Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972, which prohibits sex-based discrimination in any education program or activity receiving federal financial assistance.
events.significance: Title IX dramatically expanded opportunities for women and girls in American education and athletics and remains a cornerstone of gender equity law.

events.title: Air India Flight 182 Bombing
events.description: Air India Flight 182, flying from Montreal to London and onward to Delhi, was destroyed by a bomb off the coast of Ireland, killing all 329 people on board. A related bomb explosion at Narita Airport in Japan killed two baggage handlers the same day.
events.significance: It was the deadliest act of aviation terrorism before September 11, 2001, and led to major reforms in airport security and Canadian counterterrorism efforts.
